# Jaehyeon Kim

> Data Engineer | Data Streaming | Powering ML & AI in Real Time

Articles on data engineering, data streaming and machine learning, most with their code in a public repository. Posts in a series are listed in reading order; the other posts follow, newest first.

## Projects

- [dynamic-des documentation](https://jaehyeon.me/dynamic-des/latest/): realistic event streams from a SimPy simulation you can steer while it runs, written to Kafka, Redis, PostgreSQL, Parquet, JSONL and Iceberg
- [odctl documentation](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/): a command-line tool that runs an open-source data platform on a laptop, with Kafka, Flink, Spark, Iceberg, Trino, Airflow and MLflow wired together
- [Projects](https://jaehyeon.me/projects/): every project with its repository and posts

## Kafka Development with Docker

- [Kafka Development with Docker - Part 1 Cluster Setup](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-05-04-kafka-development-with-docker-part-1/): Set up a Kafka cluster with Docker Compose, the base for a series on developing and testing Kafka applications for AWS in containers.
- [Kafka Development with Docker - Part 2 Management App](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-05-18-kafka-development-with-docker-part-2/): Kafka management apps compared for local development, covering IAM access control and integration with MSK Connect and Glue Schema Registry.
- [Kafka Development with Docker - Part 3 Kafka Connect](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-05-25-kafka-development-with-docker-part-3/): A Kafka Connect ingestion pipeline on Docker. The MSK Data Generator creates fake customer and order records, and the Confluent S3 sink saves them.
- [Kafka Development with Docker - Part 4 Producer and Consumer](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-06-01-kafka-development-with-docker-part-4/): Kafka producer and consumer applications written in Python with kafka-python, one of several open source alternatives to the Java clients.
- [Kafka Development with Docker - Part 5 Glue Schema Registry](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-06-08-kafka-development-with-docker-part-5/): Build the Glue Schema Registry client library and use it to manage and enforce schemas in Kafka producer and consumer applications.
- [Kafka Development with Docker - Part 6 Kafka Connect with Glue Schema Registry](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-06-15-kafka-development-with-docker-part-6/): Schema registry support added to a Kafka Connect ingestion pipeline, so the source and sink connectors serialise through AWS Glue Schema Registry.
- [Producer and Consumer with Glue Schema Registry - Kafka Development with Docker Part 7](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-06-22-kafka-development-with-docker-part-7/): Schema registry support added to kafka-python producer and consumer apps, which serialise and deserialise through AWS Glue Schema Registry.
- [Kafka Development with Docker - Part 8 SSL Encryption](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-06-29-kafka-development-with-docker-part-8/): Configure TLS encryption between Kafka brokers and clients, where the client verifies the server certificate, with Java and Python examples.
- [Kafka Development with Docker - Part 9 SSL Authentication](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-07-06-kafka-development-with-docker-part-9/): Enforce two-way TLS verification so Kafka brokers check the client certificate, with Java and Python client examples of SSL authentication.
- [Kafka Development with Docker - Part 10 SASL Authentication](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-07-13-kafka-development-with-docker-part-10/): Authenticate Kafka clients with SASL instead of client certificates, with Java and Python client examples of the SASL mechanisms.
- [Kafka Development with Docker - Part 11 Kafka Authorization](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-07-20-kafka-development-with-docker-part-11/): Control user access to Kafka resources with authorization rules, keeping SASL for client authentication, with Java and Python client examples.

## Apache Beam Python Examples

- [Calculate K Most Frequent Words and Max Word Length - Apache Beam Python Examples Part 1](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-07-04-beam-examples-1/): Set up a local Apache Flink and Kafka environment, then build two Beam Python streaming pipelines for top K frequent words and longest word length.
- [Calculate Average Word Length with/without Fixed Look back - Apache Beam Python Examples Part 2](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-07-18-beam-examples-2/): Two Beam Python pipelines compute average word length from a Kafka topic, one emitting a global average and one using a sliding time window.
- [Build Sport Activity Tracker with/without SQL - Apache Beam Python Examples Part 3](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-08-01-beam-examples-3/): A sport activity tracker in Beam Python, built first with native transforms and then with Beam SQL, showing the limits of Beam SQL in the Python SDK.
- [Apache Beam Python Examples - Part 4 Call RPC Service for Data Augmentation](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-08-15-beam-examples-4/): Data augmentation in Beam Python by calling a gRPC service once per input element, running on a local Flink cluster with Kafka as the source.
- [Call RPC Service in Batch using Stateless DoFn - Apache Beam Python Examples Part 5](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-09-18-beam-examples-5/): Batching gRPC calls in a stateless DoFn so one request covers a whole bundle, cutting the time a Beam Python pipeline spends on enrichment.
- [Call RPC Service in Batch with Defined Batch Size using Stateful DoFn - Apache Beam Python Examples Part 6](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-10-02-beam-examples-6/): A stateful DoFn with Beam state and timers fixes the gRPC batch size and maximum wait time instead of leaving the bundle size to the runner.
- [Apache Beam Python Examples - Part 7 Separate Droppable Data into Side Output](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-10-24-beam-examples-7/): Late droppable elements are detected by a timer in a stateful DoFn and sent to a Beam side output instead of being discarded without notice.
- [Enhance Sport Activity Tracker with Runner Motivation - Apache Beam Python Examples Part 8](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-11-21-beam-examples-8/): Pacing messages are added to the Beam sport activity tracker by comparing short term speed metrics against their long term counterparts.
- [Develop Batch File Reader and PiSampler using Splittable DoFn - Apache Beam Python Examples Part 9](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-12-05-beam-examples-9/): Splittable DoFn in Beam Python builds a batch file reader that processes files in parallel, and a PiSampler that estimates pi by Monte Carlo runs.
- [Develop Streaming File Reader using Splittable DoFn - Apache Beam Python Examples Part 10](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-12-19-beam-examples-10/): A streaming file reader built with Splittable DoFn scans an input folder for new files repeatedly, a pattern for unbounded sources in the Python SDK.

## Real Time Streaming with Kafka and Flink

- [Real Time Streaming with Kafka and Flink - Introduction](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-10-05-real-time-streaming-with-kafka-and-flink-1/): Kafka and PyFlink replace Amazon Kinesis in a real time analytics app from an AWS workshop. The original and the new architecture are compared.
- [Produce data to Kafka using Lambda - Real Time Streaming with Kafka and Flink Lab 1](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-10-26-real-time-streaming-with-kafka-and-flink-2/): Produce fake taxi ride data into a Kafka topic on Amazon MSK from an AWS Lambda function invoked repeatedly by an EventBridge schedule rule.
- [Write data to Kafka from S3 using Flink - Real Time Streaming with Kafka and Flink Lab 2](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-11-09-real-time-streaming-with-kafka-and-flink-3/): Read records from S3 and send them into a Kafka topic with PyFlink, using a custom pipeline jar for IAM authentication, which is useful for enrichment.
- [Transform and write data to S3 from Kafka using Flink - Real Time Streaming with Kafka and Flink Lab 3](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-11-16-real-time-streaming-with-kafka-and-flink-4/): Export Kafka topic messages to S3 with PyFlink, enriching records through a user defined function and querying them on Athena through a Glue table.
- [Clean, Aggregate, and Enrich Events with Flink - Real Time Streaming with Kafka and Flink Lab 4](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-11-23-real-time-streaming-with-kafka-and-flink-5/): Aggregate taxi ride counts and trip durations by vendor over five second windows with PyFlink, then chart them in an OpenSearch dashboard.
- [Write data to DynamoDB using Kafka Connect - Real Time Streaming with Kafka and Flink Lab 5](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-11-30-real-time-streaming-with-kafka-and-flink-6/): Ingest records from a Kafka topic into a DynamoDB table using the Camel DynamoDB sink connector, defined and run on Kafka Connect.
- [Consume data from Kafka using Lambda - Real Time Streaming with Kafka and Flink Lab 6](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-12-14-real-time-streaming-with-kafka-and-flink-7/): Consume Kafka messages with an AWS Lambda function, using Amazon MSK as an event source so that Lambda polls the topic and invokes the function.

## Building Real-Time Digital Twins with dynamic-des

- [Building a Real-Time Industrial Digital Twin with Apache Flink and Online Machine Learning](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2026-04-21-digital-twin-online-machine-learning/): An Apache Flink and Kotlin streaming architecture where online machine learning detects concept drift from machinery wear, controlled by a shadow mode router.
- [Why Digital Twins Are Rewiring Industry 4.0](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2026-04-23-digital-twin-industry-4-0/): Why a simulation is not a digital twin: the layers that separate an offline model, an operational twin and an event-driven hybrid of the two.
- [Building an Event-Driven Hybrid Digital Twin with dynamic-des](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2026-04-28-digital-twin-dynamic-des/): Keeping a simulation in step with live data: change a running SimPy model's parameters from Kafka and stream its events out, so it acts as a digital twin.
- [One Simulation, Two Pipelines: Batch Training and Live Inference with Dynamic DES](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2026-05-25-dynamic-des-parquet-support/): One simulation that writes Parquet for model training and streams Kafka events for live inference, so training and serving use the same simulation code.
- [Dynamic DES: A Declarative API with Postgres and Redis Connectors](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2026-07-17-dynamic-des-declarative-connectors/): Generating test data that changes while it runs: SimPy simulations written with a declarative API that read settings from and write events to PostgreSQL and Redis.
- [Defining Data-Streaming Simulations in YAML, Without Writing Python](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2026-10-06-simulations-in-yaml-dynamic-des/): Test data for a streaming pipeline, from a settings file rather than a program: a plain YAML file describes a simulation, and one command runs it and sends its events to Kafka, PostgreSQL, Parquet or Iceberg.

## dbt Pizza Shop Demo

- [Data Build Tool (dbt) Pizza Shop Demo - Part 1 Modelling on PostgreSQL](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-01-18-dbt-pizza-shop-1/): Model fictional pizza shop data on PostgreSQL with dbt, building two SCD type 2 dimension tables and one transactional fact table.
- [Data Build Tool (dbt) Pizza Shop Demo - Part 2 ETL on PostgreSQL via Airflow](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-01-25-dbt-pizza-shop-2/): Orchestrate the PostgreSQL pizza shop dbt project with Apache Airflow, scheduling the SCD type 2 dimension and fact table builds as an ETL process.
- [Data Build Tool (dbt) Pizza Shop Demo - Part 3 Modelling on BigQuery](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-02-08-dbt-pizza-shop-3/): Model pizza shop data on Google BigQuery with dbt, keeping SCD type 2 dimensions and denormalising the fact table with nested and repeated fields.
- [Data Build Tool (dbt) Pizza Shop Demo - Part 4 ETL on BigQuery via Airflow](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-02-22-dbt-pizza-shop-4/): Orchestrate the BigQuery pizza shop dbt project with Apache Airflow, running the SCD type 2 dimension tables and the denormalised fact table.
- [Data Build Tool (dbt) Pizza Shop Demo - Part 5 Modelling on Amazon Athena](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-03-07-dbt-pizza-shop-5/): Model pizza shop data as Apache Iceberg tables transformed on Amazon Athena with dbt, using array and struct types to denormalise the fact table.
- [Data Build Tool (dbt) Pizza Shop Demo - Part 6 ETL on Amazon Athena via Airflow](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-03-14-dbt-pizza-shop-6/): Orchestrate the Amazon Athena and Iceberg pizza shop dbt project with Apache Airflow, running the dimension and denormalised fact table builds.

## Tree Based Methods in R

- [Tree Based Methods in R - Part 1](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2015-02-01-tree-based-methods-1/): Fit a CART classification model on the ISLR Carseats data with the rpart package in R, and tune the pruning parameter with the caret package.
- [Tree Based Methods in R - Part 2](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2015-02-08-tree-based-methods-2/): Cost-sensitive classification with rpart and caret in R, treating a missed High class as twice as expensive by altering the priors and the loss matrix.
- [Tree Based Methods in R - Part 3](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2015-02-14-tree-based-methods-3/): Fit a regression tree on the Carseats data in R, comparing the pruning parameter caret selects against the 1-SE rule that the rpart package recommends.
- [Tree Based Methods in R - Part 4](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2015-02-15-tree-based-methods-4/): Compare three R packages for classification trees, rpart, caret and mlr, on the Carseats data used in the earlier parts.
- [Tree Based Methods in R - Part 5](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2015-03-05-tree-based-methods-5/): Evaluate a single regression tree in R against 2000 bagged trees, comparing out-of-bag and test errors, cumulative errors and variable importance.
- [Tree Based Methods in R - Part 6](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2015-03-07-tree-based-methods-6/): Compare a single classification tree in R with 500 bagged trees on out-of-bag and test errors, cumulative errors and variable importance measures.

## Apache Beam Local Development with Python

- [Pipeline, Notebook, SQL and DataFrame - Apache Beam Local Development with Python Part 1](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-03-28-beam-local-dev-1/): Run a basic Apache Beam pipeline in Python, then develop interactively in Jupyter notebooks with Beam SQL and Beam DataFrames examples.
- [Apache Beam Local Development with Python - Part 2 Batch Pipelines](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-04-04-beam-local-dev-2/): Batch Apache Beam pipelines in Python that aggregate website visit logs by user and time, written with and without Beam SQL and run in notebooks.
- [Apache Beam Local Development with Python - Part 3 Flink Runner](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-04-18-beam-local-dev-3/): The Apache Beam portability layer explained, with bash scripts that manage local Flink and Kafka clusters and a streaming pipeline on the Flink Runner.
- [Apache Beam Local Development with Python - Part 4 Streaming Pipelines](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-05-02-beam-local-dev-4/): A streaming Apache Beam pipeline in Python that aggregates page visits by user in fixed 20 second windows, written with and without Beam SQL.
- [Apache Beam Local Development with Python - Part 5 Testing Pipelines](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-05-09-beam-local-dev-5/): Unit test batch and streaming Apache Beam pipelines in Python, using TestStream to advance watermarks and processing time across scenarios.

## dbt for Effective Data Transformation on AWS

- [Data Build Tool (dbt) for Effective Data Transformation on AWS - Part 1 Redshift](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2022-09-28-dbt-on-aws-part-1-redshift/): Transform IMDb data in Amazon Redshift Serverless with dbt, building layered models that follow dbt best practices.
- [Data Build Tool (dbt) for Effective Data Transformation on AWS - Part 2 Glue](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2022-10-09-dbt-on-aws-part-2-glue/): Transform IMDb data in an S3 data lake with dbt on AWS Glue, running layered models through Glue interactive sessions with the dbt-glue adapter.
- [EMR on EC2 - Data Build Tool (dbt) for Effective Data Transformation on AWS Part 3](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2022-10-19-dbt-on-aws-part-3-emr-ec2/): Transform IMDb data with dbt on Amazon EMR on EC2, running layered models through a Spark Thrift server.
- [EMR on EKS - Data Build Tool (dbt) for Effective Data Transformation on AWS Part 4](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2022-11-01-dbt-on-aws-part-4-emr-eks/): Transform IMDb data with dbt on Amazon EMR on EKS, through a Spark Thrift server kept running on Kubernetes by a small wrapper class.
- [Data Build Tool (dbt) for Effective Data Transformation on AWS - Part 5 Athena](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2022-12-06-dbt-on-aws-part-5-athena/): Transform IMDb data with dbt on Amazon Athena using the dbt-athena adapter, the last part of the dbt on AWS series.

## Getting Started with Real-Time Streaming in Kotlin

- [Kafka Clients with JSON - Producing and Consuming Order Events](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2025-05-20-kotlin-getting-started-kafka-json-clients/): A Kotlin Kafka producer and consumer for order events, with custom JSON serialisers, admin helpers and a Gradle build, run on odctl.
- [Kafka Clients with Avro - Schema Registry and Order Events](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2025-05-27-kotlin-getting-started-kafka-avro-clients/): Avro and Schema Registry replace hand written JSON codecs in a Kotlin Kafka producer and consumer, with generated classes and graceful shutdown.
- [Kafka Streams - Lightweight Real-Time Processing for Supplier Stats](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2025-06-03-kotlin-getting-started-kafka-streams/): Kafka Streams in Kotlin aggregates Avro order events into tumbling window supplier statistics and handles late records with a custom extractor.
- [Flink DataStream API - Scalable Event Processing for Supplier Stats](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2025-06-10-kotlin-getting-started-flink-datastream/): Flink DataStream API in Kotlin computes the same supplier statistics, using watermarks for event time and side outputs to collect late order events.
- [Flink Table API - Declarative Analytics for Supplier Stats in Real Time](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2025-06-17-kotlin-getting-started-flink-table/): Flink Table API in Kotlin states the supplier statistics as a declarative windowed aggregation over a DataStream, with late rows routed by hand.

## Kafka Connect for AWS Services Integration

- [Kafka Connect for AWS Services Integration - Part 1 Introduction](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-05-03-kafka-connect-for-aws-part-1/): A survey of the Kafka connectors available for AWS service integration, as the starting point for building real time data pipelines on AWS.
- [Develop Camel DynamoDB Sink Connector - Kafka Connect for AWS Services Integration Part 2](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-06-04-kafka-connect-for-aws-part-2/): Develop the Camel DynamoDB sink connector on Docker, consuming fake order records from a Kafka topic and writing them into a DynamoDB table.
- [Deploy Camel DynamoDB Sink Connector - Kafka Connect for AWS Services Integration Part 3](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-07-03-kafka-connect-for-aws-part-3/): Deploy the Camel DynamoDB sink connector and its data generator source on Amazon MSK and MSK Connect, moving the local pipeline onto AWS.
- [Develop Aiven OpenSearch Sink Connector - Kafka Connect for AWS Services Integration Part 4](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-10-23-kafka-connect-for-aws-part-4/): Build a local Kafka to OpenSearch pipeline on Docker with the Aiven sink connector, ingesting fake impressions and clicks for near real time analytics.
- [Deploy Aiven OpenSearch Sink Connector - Kafka Connect for AWS Services Integration Part 5](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-10-30-kafka-connect-for-aws-part-5/): Deploy a Kafka to OpenSearch pipeline on AWS with Terraform, covering a VPC, VPN server, MSK cluster, OpenSearch domain and the MSK Connect connectors.

## Serverless Data Product

- [Serverless Data Product POC Backend Part 1 - Packaging R ML Model for Lambda](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2017-04-08-serverless-data-product-1/): Package a logistic regression model built in R so it can run on AWS Lambda, after testing it locally.
- [Serverless Data Product POC Backend Part 2 - Deploying R ML Model via Lambda](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2017-04-11-serverless-data-product-2/): Deploy an R machine learning model to AWS Lambda and call it without managing a server.
- [Serverless Data Product POC Backend Part 3 - Exposing R ML Model via APIG](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2017-04-13-serverless-data-product-3/): Expose an R machine learning model packaged in AWS Lambda through Amazon API Gateway, giving the model a callable HTTP endpoint on AWS.
- [Serverless Data Product POC Backend Part 4 - Serving R ML Model via S3](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2017-04-17-serverless-data-product-4/): Host the web application that calls an R machine learning model on Amazon S3, so both the front end and the Lambda backend run without a server.

## Data Lake Demo Using Change Data Capture

- [Data Lake Demo using Change Data Capture (CDC) on AWS - Part 1 Local Development](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2021-12-05-datalake-demo-part1/): Set up the source PostgreSQL database with an outbox table, then run Debezium and an S3 sink connector locally with Docker Compose.
- [Data Lake Demo using Change Data Capture (CDC) on AWS - Part 2 Implement CDC](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2021-12-12-datalake-demo-part2/): Build change data capture on AWS with Amazon MSK and MSK Connect, streaming PostgreSQL row changes into the topics that feed the data lake.
- [Implement Data Lake - Data Lake Demo using Change Data Capture (CDC) on AWS Part 3](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2021-12-19-datalake-demo-part3/): Run a Hudi DeltaStreamer application on Amazon EMR, then query the resulting Hudi table with Athena and build a QuickSight dashboard on it.

## Getting Started with PyFlink on AWS

- [Getting Started with PyFlink on AWS - Part 1 Local Flink and Local Kafka](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-08-17-getting-started-with-pyflink-on-aws-part-1/): Develop a PyFlink app against a Kafka cluster on Docker, running it both in a virtual environment and in a local Flink cluster for better monitoring.
- [Getting Started with PyFlink on AWS - Part 2 Local Flink and MSK](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-08-28-getting-started-with-pyflink-on-aws-part-2/): Connect a PyFlink app to an IAM authenticated MSK cluster, building a custom uber jar because Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink takes only one jar.
- [Getting Started with PyFlink on AWS - Part 3 AWS Managed Flink and MSK](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-09-04-getting-started-with-pyflink-on-aws-part-3/): Deploy a PyFlink app that reads and writes Kafka topics on Amazon MSK to Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, the managed Flink runtime.

## Kafka Development on Kubernetes

- [Kafka Development on Kubernetes - Part 1 Cluster Setup](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2023-12-21-kafka-development-on-k8s-part-1/): Create a Kafka cluster on Kubernetes with Strimzi, the first step in a series on Python clients and Kafka Connect pipelines on Kubernetes.
- [Kafka Development on Kubernetes - Part 2 Producer and Consumer](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-01-04-kafka-development-on-k8s-part-2/): Send and read Kafka topic records from Python client applications built with the kafka-python package and deployed on Kubernetes.
- [Kafka Development on Kubernetes - Part 3 Kafka Connect](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-01-11-kafka-development-on-k8s-part-3/): Ingest fake customer and order data into Kafka with the MSK Data Generator and save it to S3, with connectors deployed as Strimzi custom resources.

## Parallel processing on single machine

- [Parallel Processing on Single Machine - Part 1](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2015-03-14-parallel-processing-on-single-machine-1/): Run parallel tasks on one machine in R with the snow and parallel packages, comparing clusterApply, clusterApplyLB, parLapply and parLapplyLB.
- [Parallel Processing on Single Machine - Part 2](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2015-03-17-parallel-processing-on-single-machine-2/): Loop in parallel on one machine in R with the foreach and doParallel packages, with the iterators package covered for writing the loop itself.
- [Parallel Processing on Single Machine - Part 3](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2015-03-19-parallel-processing-on-single-machine-3/): Compare the snow and foreach approaches to parallel processing in R on three practical examples, starting with k-means clustering on the Boston data.

## Realtime Dashboard with FastAPI, Streamlit and Next.js

- [Realtime Dashboard with FastAPI, Streamlit and Next.js - Part 1 Data Producer](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2025-02-18-realtime-dashboard-1/): A Python generator loads theLook eCommerce data into PostgreSQL, and a FastAPI WebSocket server queries it on a timer to serve live dashboards.
- [Streamlit Dashboard - Realtime Dashboard with FastAPI, Streamlit and Next.js Part 2](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2025-02-25-realtime-dashboard-2/): Streamlit and Apache ECharts draw a live sales dashboard that reads order counts and revenue by country from a FastAPI WebSocket server.
- [Next.js Dashboard - Realtime Dashboard with FastAPI, Streamlit and Next.js Part 3](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2025-03-04-realtime-dashboard-3/): Next.js and React with Apache ECharts show the same live order and revenue metrics, reading from the FastAPI WebSocket server in the browser.

## API development with R

- [API Development with R Part 1](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2017-11-18-api-development-with-r-1/): Serve an R function as an API three ways, with plumber, RServe and rApache, and see what each option asks of the developer to set up.
- [API Development with R Part 2](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2017-11-19-api-development-with-r-2/): Deploy plumber, RServe and rApache APIs in Docker containers, then compare the three R API options on example requests and response performance.

## dbt Guide for Production

- [DBT CI/CD Demo with BigQuery and GitHub Actions](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-09-05-dbt-cicd-demo/): GitHub Actions gives a dbt project on BigQuery a slim CI run on pull requests and a deploy job that publishes the project as a container image.
- [Guide to Running DBT in Production](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-09-13-dbt-guide/): Deploying a dbt project to dev and prod on BigQuery, covering slim CI, unit tests and a write audit publish step that builds on a cloned dataset.

## Deploy Python Stream Processing App on Kubernetes

- [Deploy Python Stream Processing App on Kubernetes - Part 1 PyFlink Application](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-05-30-beam-deploy-1/): Deploy a PyFlink application to minikube with the Flink Kubernetes Operator, alongside a Kafka cluster that provides its source and sink topics.
- [Beam Pipeline on Flink Runner - Deploy Python Stream Processing App on Kubernetes Part 2](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2024-06-06-beam-deploy-2/): Deploy an Apache Beam Python pipeline to a Flink session cluster on minikube, packaged as a Docker image and submitted as a Kubernetes job.

## Download Stock Data

- [Download Stock Data - Part I](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2014-11-20-download-stock-data-1/): Download stock price files in R, save them to a local folder and merge them into one data frame. The Google endpoint the script used has since been retired.
- [Download Stock Data - Part II](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2014-11-21-download-stock-data-2/): Download stock price data from Google in R and merge it into one data frame in memory, avoiding the slower route of saving each file to a local drive.

## From Prototype to Production: Real-Time Product Recommendation with Contextual Bandits

- [Prototyping an Online Product Recommender in Python](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2026-01-29-prototype-recommender-with-python/): A Python prototype of a contextual multi-armed bandit recommender that simulates user behaviour and validates the algorithm against cold-start users.
- [Productionizing an Online Product Recommender using Event Driven Architecture](https://jaehyeon.me/blog/2026-02-23-productionize-recommender-with-eda/): Apache Flink, Kafka and Valkey turn a contextual bandit recommender into an event driven service with stateful training and low latency inference.

## Integrate Schema Registry with MSK Connect
